meta.name: Web component stack
meta.about: The standard way a HAX web component is made: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, the four web component standards, Lit, then the HAX layer, with the tools that build and ship one and the places people learn it.

html.desc: The document: every HAX element is an HTML tag, and its content stays HTML in light DOM so it works without the element.

css.desc: Styling, scoped per element by shadow DOM and shared through DDD custom properties.

js.desc: Behavior as plain ES2020+ JavaScript; no TypeScript and no optional chaining in the monorepo.

customel.desc: customElements.define(tag, class): a new tag the browser treats as a first-class element.

shadow.desc: An element's own DOM and styles, isolated from the page; slots let authored light DOM content show through.

slots.desc: <template> and <slot>: how an element renders authored content in place.

esm.desc: import and export; one module per element, loaded on demand by the autoloader with no bundler.

lit.desc: The small library HAX elements extend: LitElement, html`` and css`` templates, reactive properties and lifecycle.

simpleicon.desc: The icon elements and iconsets HAX elements draw from, including the hax: set used in this web.

schemabeh.desc: The mixin that gives an element schema.org metadata so content is machine-readable.

tours.label: How a HAX element is built
tours.message: From the web platform to the HAX layer: what you need to know to make a web component for HAX.

scenes.caption: Everything starts from the web component standard.
Which is written in the three languages every browser speaks.
Four standards make a tag reusable: custom elements, shadow DOM, templates and slots, ES modules.
Lit is the small library HAX elements extend.
The HAX layer: DDD for style, HAXSchema for editing, i18n for languages, simple-icon and SchemaBehaviors.
The CLI scaffolds and audits one; tests, Ubiquity and SSR check and ship it.
IST 256, HAX Camp and the docs are where people learn this.
